title: Eid al-Fitr: joy
tomorrow: Eid's over. does the fasting just stop?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last ten: odd nights searched, a family woken up, a date lost in an argument. Then the moon is sighted, and the month is done.

The night the moon is spotted, phones start buzzing: Eid Mubarak, Eid Mubarak. By morning there are new clothes, a crowded prayer, and trays of sweets going door to door. And in some families, the same yearly argument: how much celebrating fits a holy day? Music or no music? The question is old. It came up in the Prophet's own house.
screen: `EID MUBARAK, EID MUBARAK.` → `HOW MUCH JOY FITS A HOLY DAY?` → `IT CAME UP IN HIS HOUSE.`

segments.voice: 'A'isha remembers an Eid, in Sahih al-Bukhari. Two girls are singing in her room. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is lying down, his face turned away. Then Abu Bakr walks in, her father, and he's upset: musical instruments of Satan, in the house of the Messenger of God? Hear his side fairly. This is a house where revelation comes down. He's guarding it, and he loves the man whose house it is. And the Prophet's answer: Abu Bakr, every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid. On another Eid, 'A'isha says, men from Abyssinia played with shields and spears, and she watched from behind him until she'd had enough. So on Eid, joy wasn't a break from religion. It was part of the day. Muslims still read that scene in more than one way. Some take it as room for song and celebration on festival days. Others note it was girls singing, on a festival, and draw the lines on music more tightly. Both start from the same room. And the joy has a door. Before the Eid prayer, the Prophet made zakat al-fitr a duty, a gift of food paid before people go out to pray, so the poor have something to eat on Eid too.
screen: `ABU BAKR: NOT IN THIS HOUSE.` · `THIS IS OUR EID.` · `ONE SCENE, TWO READINGS.` · `ZAKAT AL-FITR FIRST.` · then, large: `JOY IS WORSHIP.`

segments.voice: Eid al-Fitr: the festival of breaking the fast, the day after Ramadan. A prayer, food for the poor, and joy.
For the road: joy is worship, defended once in the Prophet's own house. Let the tables be full.

chat.meaning: When Abu Bakr objected to singing on Eid, the Prophet said every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid. Joy is part of the worship.

Eid.meaning: a festival day; Muslims keep two each year

Abu Bakr.meaning: the Prophet's closest companion, and 'A'isha's father

Abyssinia.meaning: the old name for the land of Ethiopia

zakat al-fitr.meaning: a gift of food paid before the Eid prayer

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 949–950, 952, 987 ('A'isha: two girls singing on Eid; Abu Bakr objects; 'every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid'; the Abyssinians with shields and spears)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1503 (Ibn 'Umar: zakat al-fitr made a duty, to be paid before people go out to the prayer)
Sunan Abi Dawud 1609 (zakat al-fitr as food for the poor)
